ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is the curve of the function g(x), marked with four points a, b, c, d. Point a is on the left rising branch, and the curve rises to the right but gradually becomes flatter; point b is at a relatively gentle place, after which the curve begins to become steeper; point c is on the steep rising branch to the left of the dashed line; point d is on the right descending branch. Reasoning: g'(x) being positive means the graph of the function is increasing near that point; g'(x) being decreasing means the slope becomes smaller as x increases, that is, the graph is increasing and concave down. At point a the curve is rising and the slope is becoming smaller, so it satisfies the condition. Points b and c do not meet the requirement of "slope decreasing," and the slope at point d is negative. So the answer is a.

raw_record.question_text: The graph of a function g is shown above. Which labeled point on the graph is a point where g'(x) is positive and decreasing?

method.method_draft: Inspect the labeled points on the graph: point a lies on the left rising branch where the curve is increasing but bending downward/flattening; point b is on a nearly flat portion beginning to bend upward; point c is on the steep rising branch before the dashed vertical line; point d is on the right branch where the graph is decreasing. Use the text condition that g'(x) must be positive and decreasing. Positive g'(x) means the graph of g is increasing at that point, and decreasing g'(x) means the slopes are getting smaller as x increases, i.e. the graph is concave down. The only labeled point that is both increasing and concave down is a.

method.method_draft: Compare the tangent slopes just to the left and just to the right of each labeled point. Around d, the tangent slope is negative because the graph descends. Therefore the labeled point satisfying positive and decreasing derivative is a.
